headline: Apple seeks Trump admin approval for Chinese RAM after product price increases
summary: Apple is reportedly seeking an exemption from the Trump administration to buy memory chips from a blacklisted Chinese supplier, aiming to mitigate rising product costs.
details: Apple is reportedly seeking a waiver from the Trump administration to procure memory chips from a blacklisted Chinese supplier. This move comes as the company faces increasing product prices.

The request, reported by The Financial Times, highlights the challenges Apple faces in navigating complex international trade policies and supply chain disruptions. Securing these chips could help manage manufacturing costs.
The supplier in question is on a US government blacklist, making direct transactions difficult without special approval. This situation underscores the broader tensions in US-China tech trade.

If approved, this could provide Apple with a crucial alternative source for components, potentially impacting the pricing and availability of its future products. The decision rests with the administration.

headline_marked: [[Zero-cost AI video generator]] built with Agnes AI offers full features for free
headline: Zero-cost AI video generator built with Agnes AI offers full features for free
summary: A new open-source tool leverages Agnes AI to provide script writing, image synthesis, video rendering, voiceover, and subtitles at no cost, requiring only a free API key.
details: A developer has created a truly zero-cost AI video generator, leveraging Agnes AI's models. Unlike most services that charge monthly or per-second, this tool offers script writing, image synthesis, video rendering, voiceover, and subtitles entirely free, requiring only a free API key from Agnes AI.

The project aims to make AI video creation more equitable, addressing the current high barrier to entry for industrial-grade video generation. While Agnes's video model is still evolving, this initiative provides an accessible way for ordinary users to experiment and create.

The generator offers multiple modes: a Simple Video API wrapper for testing, a Creative Video mode that expands story ideas into multi-scene videos with visual continuity, and a Manuscript Video & Digital Anchor mode for long articles or scripts, auto-splitting and generating video segments with unified narration and subtitles.

Users can run the tool locally by cloning the GitHub repository and following a simple `start.sh` script. It creates a virtual environment, installs dependencies, and starts a local server, accessible via `http://localhost:8765`. An Agnes AI API key is needed for operation.

This project aligns with Agnes AI founder Bruce Yang's vision of making world-class AI accessible to everyone. It requires no subscription, no expensive GPU, just a free API key and a Python-capable machine, contributing to democratizing AI video creation.
